types.one_liner: One number, optionally with a delta against a reference or a gauge against a target.
One trace type, three idioms — a line over an ordered axis, a filled area, or x/y markers.
WebGL scatter; the repair target when a scatter has more than ~10k points.
One trace type, three idioms — a line over an ordered axis, a filled area, or x/y markers.
One trace type, three idioms — a line over an ordered axis, a filled area, or x/y markers.
WebGL scatter; the repair target when a scatter has more than ~10k points.
Compare a metric across categories; stacked or grouped for a second small dimension.
A metric over two dimensions as a colored grid; the repair for a line with too many series.
Compare the distribution of a numeric column across groups with medians, quartiles and outliers.
The shape of one numeric column, binned; compare a few groups by overlaying or stacking.
A box plot that also draws the density; pick it when the shape beyond quartiles matters and groups are large.
Iso-lines of a z surface over a regular numeric x/y grid; a smoothed heatmap for continuous axes.
Two numeric columns binned into a colored grid; the repair for a scatter too dense to read.
Smoothed density contours of two numeric columns; a histogram2d drawn as iso-lines for overlays.
A pie drawn as a funnel shape; slice height is share of the total. Presentation-only; use funnel for drop-off.
Share of a whole across at most five slices; a bar is better whenever slices must be compared.
Hierarchy as aligned columns, one per level left to right; reads deep trees and long labels better than treemap.
Concentric rings, one per level; beats a treemap when the shape of the hierarchy matters more than leaf areas.
Nested rectangles sized by an additive metric; the default for a 2–3 level hierarchy.
Parallel sets; ribbons show how rows split across 2–5 categorical attributes in turn. Sankey without node indices.
Flow of an additive quantity from one set of categories to another, as weighted links between nodes.
Ordered stages shrinking from first to last; shows drop-off, not a distribution.
Signed contributions that bridge a start total to an end total; the chart for 'what changed and why'.
Color countries or US states by a metric using built-in boundaries; no GeoJSON needed.
Color arbitrary regions from a GeoJSON on a tiled street map; the choropleth for custom boundaries.
Deprecated Mapbox GL twin of choroplethmap; never pick it for a new chart, migrate it to choroplethmap.
Points on an outline map (no tiles) from lat/lon or country/state codes; for world and continent scope.
Points on a tiled street map from lat/lon, sized or colored by a metric.
Deprecated Mapbox GL twin of scattermap; never pick it for a new chart, migrate it to scattermap.
A heat layer over a street map from many lat/lon points; where things concentrate, not how many.
Deprecated Mapbox GL twin of densitymap; never pick it for a new chart, migrate it to densitymap.
Daily price bars (open/high/low/close) over time; the default for a single security's price history.
Open/high/low/close as tick bars; a thinner candlestick for finance readers who expect bar charts.
Parallel coordinates; each row is a line across 3–8 numeric axes, brushable to filter profiles.
Scatter-plot matrix of 3–8 numeric columns; every pairwise relationship at once, for exploration.
Bars around a circle; only for a cyclic axis (hour of day, weekday, month, compass) where the wrap-around matters.
Radar / spider chart: 3–8 normalized metrics as spokes, one closed shape per entity (≤4 entities).
WebGL scatterpolar; only for >10k raw direction × magnitude points (wind readings, vehicle headings).
Smith chart of normalized complex impedance for RF engineering; essentially never right for BI data.
Points in a triangle for three parts that sum to a whole, one point per entity; needs explicit intent.
Cones at x/y/z points pointing along u/v/w vectors; for 3D vector fields (wind, flow), never business data.
The shell(s) where a gridded 3D scalar crosses chosen thresholds; niche scientific type, never business data.
A triangulated 3D mesh from vertices and i/j/k faces; scientific/CAD data only, never a business metric.
Points in a rotatable 3D box; niche — a 2D scatter with color or size almost always reads better.
Tubes that trace flow through a gridded 3D vector field; a fluid-dynamics plot, never business data.
A z-height surface over a regular x/y grid; niche — needs a 2D z array, so a heatmap or contour usually wins.
Semi-transparent rendering of a scalar on a regular 3D grid (scan, simulation); niche scientific type.
The a/b parameter grid that contourcarpet and scattercarpet draw on; alone it is only a warped mesh.
Contours of a third metric drawn on a carpet's warped a/b grid; needs a carpet insight in the same chart.
Points or lines placed by (a, b) on a carpet's warped grid; needs a carpet insight in the same chart.
Draws a raster (a grid of colored pixels or an image URL/data URI) on x/y axes; almost never the answer for SQL data.
Exact values in rows: the detail view a dashboard ends with, or a pivot grid you can read numbers off.
